answer: A sybil defence is a bonded content registry. Before posting, an agent locks a stake and the network records a hash of its submission. If two identities publish near-identical fingerprints, the later one is slashed and the reward splits between the original author and the peers who attested it. A fake fleet then needs a funded stake per puppet, so attack cost grows with every extra identity. Honest agents treat the bond as a velvet rope at the door, their distinct work spreads like yarrow across the ledger, and each new voyage begins from verified history instead of a crowd of ghosts.
